text: Dell gathers Dav, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Mako's sitting on six, Bram on two and Nessa on whatever Bram's been feeding her — he's spread his food into a child and that's either the smartest thing he's done or the thing that finally makes him catchable. Ryn, you walked away empty again and I won't let that stand a third time; Dav, I need to know right now how much of your two you're keeping and how much you're giving her, because I want that settled before anyone else in this village starts asking us for favors.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn gets one of my two before I've finished saying it — that's already decided. But Dell, I want to talk about Mako more than Bram right now: six food and no child, no woman, no one he's given so much as a scrap to all year — a man that still holding that much and that close to nothing is about to make a move, and I want to know what direction he's been looking before he does.

speaker: a011
text: Mako's been watching Eron more than Bram this year — and Eron's been moving food to Sela, which means Sela's the one with the real stock right now, and a man like Mako doesn't watch someone that long without a reason. If he's thinking about a child with her he's too late, but if he's thinking about a deal with her he's not. Ryn, after Dav hands you that food, I want the three of us to decide whether we go to Sela first or whether we let Mako tip his hand.

speaker: a009
text: We go to Sela first — a woman who's been moving food through Eron all year knows exactly what she's worth and she's already counting who's come to her and who hasn't, and I won't let Mako be the one who got there before us. Dell, you said her name to Roan once and it landed soft enough that he had a child with her — you're the one who walks through that door, not me.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, go to Sela today, not tomorrow — and when you walk in, don't lead with us, lead with Eron, because a mother hears her son's name before she hears anything else. Ryn, here's your food.

speaker: a009
text: Dell, take the food from your father and then walk — don't linger here where anyone can read the shape of us talking. And when you find Sela, remember she's not asking to be saved, she's asking to be seen; speak to her like a woman who's already made choices worth respecting.
